acceptance: Build a real wheel and install into a clean isolated environment outside either checkout; run CLI/local fixture review and gate scenarios using installed templates and data, not PYTHONPATH source imports.

Two consumer policies with distinct App login/attesters/base branches accept their own trusted identity and reject each other's identity; missing configuration fails clearly, never defaults to BenchBox.

Wrong hash, missing dependency hash, tampered source, absent artifact and mismatched warm cache refuse before executing bytes; blocking primary URL selects only the retained identical bytes, wrong secondary hash refuses.

Matcher executes under python -I -S against a non-BenchBox manifest with no import-time file access. Base/PR manifest disagreement cannot narrow required heavy tier; vendored drift is detected if chosen.
Package metadata/dependency/runtime contract and public install/API docs are updated; required tests, installer smoke and reviewed PR merge pass.

One lock/bootstrap contract covers CI, local/cloud sessions, gate and pr-arm; lock includes exact asset URLs and workflow revision. Installation key includes artifact/dependency hashes, interpreter and platform. Verify installed executable content or recreate from verified bytes; a directory/marker alone never proves a valid install.

Interrupted install, hostile PR-local module/package, changed trusted manifest, corrupt installed executable and trusted-ref refresh failure all refuse or reconstruct safely from verified exact artifacts; both bytes and dependencies are verified before execution.
Persisted finding/dispute state is preserved/imported explicitly; retry/attempt/cache and provenance formats keep defined compatibility. Old export directories become inert without deleting findings.
context:
T3; resolves P4/R1/R5 installer obligations. Lock/schema locations are determined by the ADR and existing project patterns, not arbitrary names in this item. Existing local cache validity includes trusted package/policy/manifest/config digest; preserve that property.

Delivery: one Theseus PR (Theseus PR 1) carries governance bootstrap, package/installer, hosted workflows, local tooling, frozen source and parity proof. The release tag and first-promotion evidence come from that merged head, not from a separate PR.

Owner (2026-11-03): the Theseus repository is https://github.com/joeharris76/theseus, replacing the planned BenchBox-dev/theseus. Live check: exists, private, MIT, default branch main, one initial commit 392e84d (LICENSE, README.md, .gitignore); admin access confirmed.

Delivered: theseus-reviewer package with consumer-configured identity (bot_login, gated_base, attesters from trusted policy) and hash-verified isolated installer (theseus PRs #1, #6, #8 pin bound to lock, #9 Windows bootstrap, #11 code-owned seams). Vendored into BenchBox as _project/scripts/theseus_bootstrap.py, byte-identical to v0.1.4.
description:
Build the real reviewer/gate package in Theseus: dist theseus-reviewer, import theseus_reviewer, CLI theseus. Include templates and all runtime files from the inventory. Configure App login, attesters, gated base and policy/manifest paths from trusted consumer policy; the wheel carries no BenchBox identity, branch, or path defaults. Gate identity must actually use configured values rather than ignore bot_login.
Implement a minimal consumer bootstrap that resolves a lock from a trusted consumer commit, verifies downloaded bytes and the complete dependency closure, and installs into an isolated environment. Record immutable source commit, wheel/dependency hashes, runtime constraints and two independent byte sources. Verify before execution; cache identity is the exact hash/version. No latest, ambient install, source-build hooks from PRs, or cache fallback to a different version. Recovery source must be readable by clean CI without credentials and serve the identical hash. Lock-parser/verifier trust must come from the consumer base, never the candidate.
Implement the matcher arrangement selected by its owner decision. Recommended single stdlib-only, import-pure module takes explicit manifest input; BenchBox-specific validation regex and override lookups stay outside it. If vendored, only one byte-identical copy is allowed and lock binds its digest.
Guardrails: no compatibility shims or dual independently maintained matcher; no branding-driven marker/status/cache-schema renames; preserve notices and lazy imports; no production package publication here. No BenchBox callsite deletion until atomic cutover. Worktree, comment-policy and normal reviewed-PR rules apply.
